live_handoff: SESSION 2026-07-26 #8: FOREST-CARRIERS S5 COMPLETE + RELEASED v0.50.0 (develop; master stays v0.48.0) — `-static-libmadc` / THE AOT LEDGER. WHAT: a program using try/catch/throw or a VLA needed libmadc.so.0 at run time, and on Mach-O — where no madc library exists — could not be emitted AT ALL. `madc -static-libmadc -o prog prog.c` now merges the runtime pieces the program actually uses into its own image (gcc -static-libgcc precedent; `-static` = alias; libc/libstdc++ stay dynamic). THE LEDGER = DUAL-BUILD SOURCES: the C-lane runtime moved to src/rt/rt_except.c (whole SJLJ try/throw/catch + cleanup) and src/rt/rt_vla.c. The HOST build compiles them into libmadc via $(CXX) -x c -std=c11 (NOT a separate $(CC) — every MODE's target/sysroot flags live in CXX, e.g. hosted darwin's clang++-18 -target ... --sysroot), and MADC COMPILES THE SAME SOURCES THROUGH c2mir at pack time into MIR ledger modules. ONE implementation, two consumers; scripts/ledger_sources.txt is the SINGLE OWNER of the list, read by src/Makefile (RT_LEDGER_SRCS/RT_OFILES, with $(error) if empty), forest_pack.sh and forest_pack_darwin.sh. TIER-A MEMBERSHIP RULE (sharper than 'C-compilable'): strict C11, NO compiler builtins — madc lowers __builtin_x to __madc_x, so a builtin shim compiled BY madc calls straight back into itself. That is why exception_runtime.cpp's __atomic_* wrappers moved to va_helpers.cpp beside the bswap/ffs/clz/popcount/overflow shims, and why that whole family stays TIER B until madc lowers those builtins to native MIR ops. MIR HAS NO TLS (and madc's own parser rejects _Thread_local): the source uses a MADC_RT_TLS macro = _Thread_local for the host build, EMPTY for the ledger build, so a -static-libmadc image carries PROCESS-GLOBAL exception state (Tier-3 floor gap; documented in the man page). CARRIER: new OPTIONAL container segment CIR_FOREST_SEG_LEDGER (=21) / SNAP_KIND_CIR_LEDGER (=CONSUMER+22) — header + directory + per-module symbol index + .bmir bytes; rides every carrier the forest rides for free; NO format-version bump (optional-by-design, absent = no ledger = loud refusal, like the MIR module cache). READ INDEPENDENTLY OF THE GROVE BIND: the chain was factored into ONE walker Program::probe_forest_chain(require_config_match, cfg_mismatch) — the grove bind passes true (v27 producer-config gate), the ledger passes FALSE, because madc's own runtime is target-specific but DIALECT-AGNOSTIC (a --std=c99 compile that cannot bind the groves must still link the runtime; --no-forest-bind means 'parse headers live', not 'leave the runtime out'). Program::ensure_ledger_forest() reuses bind_forest when it opened, else re-walks; SILENT on failure — the emit lane owns the diagnostic. EMIT: cir_ledger_pull() runs BEFORE MIR_link (object mode only), transitive to a fixpoint, WHOLE modules (gcc .a-member granularity), so eager object-mode gen puts the code in the capture; cir_static_libmadc_verify() at emit then confirms nothing madc-side is left and drops the DT_NEEDED unconditionally. TWO DISTINCT DIAGNOSTICS (never conflate): 'no ledger reached the pull' = BUILD-side (use a packed/installed madc, or --forest-bind=<file>) vs the TIER-B refusal listing the symbols. THREE BUGS FIXED, each at its own layer: (a) the ledger compile made its own Programs the ACTIVE owner of the process-global token/value/type pools (build_tu_module -> activate_token_pools) and then destroyed them, so the caller's freeze interned into freed memory (SIGSEGV in cir_freeze_forest -> intern_table::intern) — a side excursion OWNS restoring the previously-active Program (`restore` param); (b) every ledger function got a __madc_shim_<sym> MadValue adapter importing madc_value_* — exactly the libmadc dependency the flag removes — fixed with the EXISTING aot_skip_eval_shims knob; (c) COVER ANALYSIS, TWICE: native — dlsym+dladdr answers 'where does the process's WINNING definition live', and stderr is COPY-RELOCATED into bin/madc's own .bss, so it looked uncovered and EVERY AOT program touching stderr kept a needless libmadc.so.0; the cover libraries are now asked directly (dlopen(soname, RTLD_LAZY|RTLD_NOLOAD) + dlsym) before the dladdr fallback. CROSS — a cross build's target libs are NOT the host's; darwin's stderr is __stderrp, absent from glibc, so the emit refused; under MADC_CROSS_TARGET the check is now 'does LIBMADC define this?' (libmadc is loaded in this very process) and anything else belongs to the target system, surfacing at ITS loader — the ordinary cross-compiler contract (native is preprocessor-excluded). CRAFT NOTE: setjmp IN A LOOP is UB at -O2 (automatics modified after the setjmp are indeterminate after a longjmp) — both MIR error brackets (cir_ledger_read_module, cir_ledger_write_module) live in their OWN frames so the caller's loop state is never corrupted; apply this whenever arming cir_mir_error_jmp inside iteration. GATE: permanent scripts/forest_ledger_gate.sh in fulltest — 14 checks over a container the gate freezes ITSELF with --freeze-ledger= (the same call the release pack makes); a BASELINE LEG PER PROGRAM (it must keep libmadc.so.0 WITHOUT the flag) is what stops the -static-libmadc legs passing vacuously; --dump-forest gained ledger/ledgermod lines as the assertion surface. VALIDATION (all green, on committed content): fulltest 756/0/0/9 + forest_ledger_gate OK, --exe 740/0, packed arbiter 756/0/0/9; PRODUCT path — make release packs bin/madc-release = 240 units + ledger (2 modules / 22 symbols), that binary emits a try/catch program with ZERO libmadc DT_NEEDED and it runs under env -i LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/nonexistent; DARWIN up to the hardware line (cross-emitted from Linux, both arches) — forest_pack_darwin.sh carries the ledger and now FAILS the pack without one, and the same program that still refuses without the flag emits a valid Mach-O 64-bit arm64 / x86_64 executable (NOUNDEFS|DYLDLINK|TWOLEVEL|PIE) with zero libmadc strings and zero undefined __madc_*. STATED BOUNDARIES: (i) RUNNING an emitted Mach-O still needs the owner's Mac (the AMFI leg), like every S1-S3 darwin leg; (ii) the .o LINK lane refuses -static-libmadc loudly — the ledger merges into a compile CONTEXT, that lane merges native relocatables through MIR_object_read, which needs the fork's MH_OBJECT flavor (task #4); (iii) the builtin-shim family stays Tier B. NEXT (forest-carriers plan): S6 madc.ini — the LAST carriers slice (configure-gated --enable-config-file, OFF for embedding hosts; precedence CLI > env > ini > baked; fills discovery arm 5). ALSO QUEUED: MH_OBJECT .o flavor (task #4, fork); darwin dylib packaging shape; DK_FPTR arena kind (darwin sig_t); __builtin_va_list char* arm64-darwin; C-lane c++/v1 search order + libc++ parse burn-down + libc++ STD-ABI mangled-direct flavor (P2, owner-confirmed order: carriers first); prelude growth (sockets); Windows/PE. Deferred residue (LOW): re-signer for rewriting EXISTING signed Mach-O. KNOWN CRUFT: docs/build.md is stale (still documents asmjit) — a small cleanup candidate. STANDING: QNAP never builds/tests (container ssh -p 2299 dev@localhost does ALL; payloads need explicit cd /workspace/madc; capture rc before piping); git commit -F; never git add -A (owner WIP __c-tests-temp.*); cap every test run; one heavy container job (detached nohup runner + rc-file Monitor); CLI flags BEFORE inputs; A QUESTION IS NEVER A DIRECTIVE; SDK NEVER committed/synced; configure is GENERATED/untracked (autoconf in the container after a configure.ac change); frozen forest = THE precompiled-header model BOTH platforms; embedded live-parse = fallback lane + freeze-time input ONLY. REHYDRATE: scripts/resume.sh -> this live_handoff -> docs/plans/2026-07-25-forest-carriers-plan.md (S1+S2+S3+S4+S5 stamped) -> S6.

known_pre_existing_gaps: FIXED 2026-06-12 (this session): multi-declarator ctor-init hang (`Q a(1), b(2);` — ctor-syntax decl path now does the standard comma-continuation; tests/testctorcomma.mad); VLA-variable sizeof returned 8 for 1D AND multidim AND typedef VLA vars (runtime dims now captured into hidden __madc_vla_dim_* locals at declaration, sizeof(var) builds the runtime product; tests/testvlasizeof.mad); global const array dim read 0 (parse-time-known const scalar int initializers now baked into var->data + vfCONSTBAKED admits the CIR read-fold so `const int H=G+3;` emits a constant file-scope initializer; tests/testconstdim.mad); testfortypedcomma flake not reproducible at live HEAD (25 consecutive green runs) — resolved by intervening parser work.

VLA sizeof in CONSTANT-required contexts (e.g. `int b[sizeof(vla_a)]`) still folds to 8 via the constant evaluate_type_query path (the expression-path fix doesn't reach it); alignof(vla_var) still reports pointer alignment 8 (gcc: element alignment). Same family, much rarer.

VLA NOT DEALLOCATED ON BACKWARD GOTO: a `goto` jumping back to before a VLA's declaration must deallocate the VLA (gcc/C semantics; gcc-torture 20040811-1.c). madc lowers VLAs as malloc + __attribute__((cleanup)), which frees only on SCOPE EXIT, not on the backward goto re-entering the scope — so a backward-goto loop over a VLA LEAKS one allocation per iteration. 20040811-1.c leaks ~2GB over 1e6 iterations; it passes only when memory is available (it OOM-SIGSEGV'd when the MIR fork's 128MB code-holder reservation reduced headroom — see mir_fork; arch-gated off x86-64, so it passes again). Proper fix: free the VLA at the backward goto. Separate future slice.

MadArray/MadValue namespacing is an open API/ABI follow-up: moving the real C++ types to madc::array and madc::value would give PHP array helpers a normal namespace type surface, but compatibility aliases alone will not preserve old C++ mangled names.

Embedded <iostream> output remains partially staged: cout/cerr/clog still use header-defined stdio-backed ostream bodies. Follow-up is to replace that output surface with real libstdc++ declarations/operators, matching the std::cin direction; do not add stdio.h/FILE* stream bridges.
Real system-header PCH regeneration is deferred until PCH preserves include-guard/macro state; broad regenerated blobs currently duplicate transitive typedefs/declarations.

Explicit --std=c++ real iostream preprocessing reaches c2mir but fails on unresolved class/member aliases such as char_type, iter_type, iostate, __streambuf_type, __ostream_type, and __ios_type. Fix this generically through class/member alias resolution, not per-std shims.
